title: Titanium Coilover Spring
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, UNS R56400) was selected for this suspension application because its 900+ MPa tensile enables thin-wall lightweighting under cyclic loading. The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by high-performance racing coil suspension spring (beta-c) and specific design requirements.
process: CNC turn-mill multi-axis for suspension geometry
Shot peening Almen with SPC sampling
Black oxide/DLC coating with SPC sampling
CMM SPC dimensional check with SPC sampling
surfaceTreatment: DLC coating 2um, 15GPa hardness, 0.1mu friction coefficient applied to wear surfaces for extended durability — tailored for highperformance racing coil application
commonFailures: Fatigue crack at thread-shank transition - prevented by larger fillet R0.5->1.5mm + cold rolling — critical for highperformance racing coil performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Coilover Spring suitable for High-performance racing coil suspension spring (Beta-C)?
faq.a: Titanium Coilover Spring uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address suspension operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Coilover Spring?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Coilover Spring is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for highperformance racing coil requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Coilover Spring require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. highperformance racing coil components require DLC coating 2um, 15GPa hardness, 0.1mu friction coefficient applied to wear surfaces for extended durability — tailored for highperformance racing coil application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Coilover Spring shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Coilover Spring includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet highperformance racing coil specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Coil spring / Race spring suspension components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
